evidence.title: Federal Reserve Total Assets
evidence.summary: The snapshotted target change was -0.278 percent; it resolved to 'yes'.

evidence.title: Fed Balance Sheet QT: -$37 Billion in November, -$2.43 Trillion from Peak, to $6.54 Trillion | Crypto Craft
evidence.summary: This source directly states the Fed's balance sheet declined by $37 billion in November 2024 to $6.53 trillion and that QT ended on December 1, 2024. This provides a direct measurement of the balance sheet immediately prior to the target period and indicates a significant policy shift.

evidence.title: Jerome Powell’s December 18, 2024 Press Conference – Notable Aspects
evidence.summary: This source indicates that the Federal Reserve lowered the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point on December 18, 2024, and that policy is now 'significantly less restrictive.' While not directly about the balance sheet, a less restrictive monetary policy stance could influence future balance sheet decisions or the pace of any remaining QT.

evidence.title: STIR: FED Reverse Repo Year-End Operation Usage J...- 12-31-2024 | MNI
evidence.summary: This source indicates a jump in Reverse Repo (RRP) usage at year-end 2024. While RRP operations are distinct from the balance sheet, changes in RRP usage can reflect liquidity conditions and the Fed's management of short-term rates, which are related to overall monetary policy and could indirectly influence balance sheet dynamics.

evidence.title: Chronology of Fed’s Quantitative Easing • Yardeni Research
evidence.summary: This source provides historical context on the Fed's balance sheet normalization principles, including the intention to conclude the reduction of aggregate securities holdings by the end of September 2019. While dated, it establishes the historical precedent and policy framework for ending balance sheet reduction, which is relevant given the 'QT ended on December 1' statement.

evidence.title: Fed’s Balance Sheet Reduction Reaches $402 Billion | Wolf Street
evidence.summary: This source details the mechanics of the Fed's balance sheet reduction (QT) in 2018, explaining that the Fed sheds assets by allowing them to 'roll off' without replacement. This provides crucial background on how QT operates, which is relevant to understanding the 'QT ended' statement for December 2024.

evidence.title: This is how the Fed Has Been Sneak-Tightening Notch by Notch | Wolf Street
evidence.summary: This source discusses the subtle shrinkage of the Fed's balance sheet in 2015-2016, even while the Fed was still replacing maturing securities. It highlights that balance sheet changes can occur incrementally and sometimes without explicit announcements, providing historical context for how balance sheet adjustments can be perceived or implemented.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
evidence.summary: This FOMC statement from December 2014 outlines the Fed's policy of reinvesting principal payments from its holdings to maintain accommodative financial conditions. This historical policy stance provides a contrast to the 2024 situation where QT was ending, illustrating the Fed's varying approaches to balance sheet management over time.
